newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rotterdam dockers back at work, dispute unresolved.
newsitem.headline: Rotterdam dockers back at work, dispute unresolved.

text.p: Workers of the Rotterdam port labour pool company SHB were back at work on Friday, although there was still no settlement to the dispute which sparked a strike earlier this week, a company manager said.
"There is no strike at the moment. They are at work, although they are waiting for discussions with their union," the manager said.
No-one from the union was available for comment.
The Rotterdam port authority said on Friday ships were moving in and out of the port as normal.
Oil traders in the Rotterdam area said loading and unloading of crude and oil products also appeared unaffected.
"(The strike has had) no effect at all," one trader said.
The dispute centres around plans by SHB's management to make 275 of its 975 employees redundant and to put 375 workers on a three-day week.
On Thursday, the dispute escalated with some 300 workers on strike, but the port itself and individual companies were largely unaffected.
